extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users and authors preparing mathematical documents (AMS authors, TeX maintainers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for installing, upgrading, and using AMS-LaTeX (amsmath, amscls and related packages), including prerequisites, recommended installation/upgrade practices, available documentation, and auxiliary packages for authors of mathematical documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working TeX system (prerequisite)
rubrics_metrics.description: A working TeX system is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX is not an AMS product. See the AMS TeX Resources page for sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current LaTeX system dated December 2000 or later
rubrics_metrics.description: You need a current working LaTeX system, dated December 2000 or later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LaTeX is not an AMS product; see the LaTeX Project home page for information if you do not already have LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not re-install AMS-LaTeX on modern TeX distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: If your system is based on TeX Live (or MiKTeX or MacTeX) later than 2005, AMS-LaTeX is included as part of the LaTeX 'required' collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should not have to download or install AMS-LaTeX separately on such distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS-LaTeX consists of two components
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS-LaTeX has two components: the document classes (amscls) and the amsmath package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They can be obtained separately if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: amscls installation behavior and upgrade recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The amscls archive will unpack into an existing TEXMF structure and in most cases provide a ready-to-use installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended method for upgrading is to upgrade the entire TeX Live installation rather than installing amscls separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: amsmath authoritative source and maintenance note
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath is the extension package providing math features; responsibility for its maintenance was transferred to the LaTeX Project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authoritative version of amsmath is on CTAN and in TeX Live (note: LuaTeX v1 issues motivated the maintenance transfer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of amsmath
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath provides various features to facilitate writing math formulas and to improve the typographical quality of their output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use amsmath for enhanced math typesetting and typographical improvements over base LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of amscls (document classes and theorem package)
rubrics_metrics.description: amscls contains AMS document class files (amsart, amsbook and amsproc.cls) and a theorem package (amsthm.sty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These can be used independently and provide the setup necessary to give a LaTeX document the general structure and appearance of an AMS article or book.

rubrics_metrics.name: amsfonts / amssymb for extended symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: amsfonts is a collection of fonts that extends the Computer Modern family with additional symbols and alphabets intended for mathematical contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full LaTeX support is provided by the included amssymb and several script-specific packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: amsrefs for bibliographic organization
rubrics_metrics.description: amsrefs is an extension package for LaTeX that supports the organization and formatting of bibliographic information directly within a document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use amsrefs when you want AMS-style bibliography management inside the LaTeX source.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to view package documentation (texdoc)
rubrics_metrics.description: To view documentation for a package in an installation based on TeX Live, use the 'texdoc -l package_name' command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The desired item can be selected from the offered list. If texdoc is not installed or documentation was omitted, use TeXdoc Online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Math Guide recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Short Math Guide for LaTeX is a concise summary of the essential features in LaTeX for writing math formulas, including features provided by amssymb and amsmath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not a mere listing but a careful selection of LaTeX commands especially recommended for authors' use, with discussion of common uses and misuses to avoid for typographical quality or logical markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from technical notes and sample files
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation includes technical notes, a user's guide, and sample papers illustrating package usage (e.g., technote, testmath, subeqn, thmtest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This material is best understood when the source and output are examined side by side; sample source and output files are provided for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use amsmidx or imakeidx for multiple indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmidx.sty is a package for use with document classes based on amsbook.cls to produce multiple indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions are in amsmidx.pdf; the package imakeidx is an approved alternative to amsmidx.

rubrics_metrics.name: amsbooka.sty for multi-author books
rubrics_metrics.description: amsbooka.sty is for books that contain chapters written by individual authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This package will properly format tables of contents as well as the chapter headings for such multi-author books.
